Subject: POC preflight: environment logistics & ownership (MAP draft)

Sam — thanks again for taking time this morning. Quick recap from our call and a proposed Mutual Action Plan (MAP) milestone focused on the POC environment so we can align owners and dependencies. Please review and confirm or flag edits.

High-level objective:
- Run a 2-week POC of Redwood inference (hosted -> dedicated path) against a representative clinical ingestion pipeline and measure latency/cost at 95th pct.

POC milestone: Environment readiness (target completion: 2 weeks from MAP sign)
- Required items (dependencies): VPC peering (or secure egress), IP allowlist for Redwood egress IPs, SSO/SAML for SSO-authenticated admin console, secrets/KMS access pattern for service-to-service keys, minimal firewall/NAT rules for inference egress, service account provisioning.
- Proposed owners: AquilaHealth IT (network & SSO), Redwood (service onboarding & config), AquilaHealth App team (test data subset + schema).
- Target close for POC: 2026-05-01 (flexible if procurement gating).
- Blockers: Procurement PO, KMS access SLA (if using customer KMS), internal change window for VPC peering.

Next steps (action items):
1) I will share a short MAP spreadsheet that lists milestones + owner columns (attached).
2) Sam / Priya: confirm which of these you own vs want Redwood to own by EOD Wednesday.
3) AquilaHealth IT: please confirm whether you prefer VPC peering or IP allowlist-based egress; if peering, provide VPC IDs and a maintenance window.
4) Laura: I looped you for SSO/SAML onboarding and secrets/KMS flow options.

Attachments: Redwood_MAP_AquilaHealth_v1.xlsx (MAP draft), redwood-poc-network-requirements.pdf (network checklist).

Attaching MAP v1 with a milestone-level RACI and a short network playbook. Answers inline to Sam’s asks: 

- Redwood egress/peering notes: If you choose VPC peering, Redwood will provide a managed peering endpoint; peering is routed (no egress IP allowlist required for traffic inside peering). If you choose to keep public egress, we provide a static egress IP block (see attachment: redwood-poc-network-requirements.pdf). Either approach supports KV cache and streaming traffic; peered path is preferred for PHI-sensitive traffic.
- NAT: Peering path will not require NAT for the peered subnets; however, if your peering uses overlapping CIDRs we'll need to either modify routes or use a transit setup.
- Test data / ingestion: Attached sample ingestion script (s3 -> Redwood proxy) and recommended test size: 100–500 records (1–10MB total) to validate latency/cost at low cost.

Please see the attached MAP spreadsheet: I added target dates per your windows (peering week 4/19, SAML metadata by 4/7). Please update the owner column if anything’s off.

Attachments: Redwood_MAP_AquilaHealth_v1.xlsx, redwood-poc-network-requirements.pdf, sample-ingest.py (attachment stub).

Ben
